newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tractors Malaysia sees muted impact from duties.
newsitem.headline: Tractors Malaysia sees muted impact from duties.

text.p: Tractors Malaysia Holdings Bhd does not expect to see a big impact on its earnings from Malaysia's proposal to reimpose import duties on heavy equipment, its managing director said on Tuesday.
"From the way the economy is developing, the year ahead looks as promising as before," Oh Teik Tatt told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
In its 1997 budget, Malaysia proposed reimposing import duties of between five and 20 percent on heavy equipment in order to spur development of the local construction machinery industry.
Tractors Malaysia sells new and used construction equipment and has distribution rights for BMW and Ford cars.
Oh said the duties proposal "is going to have some impact on our heavy equipment business", but added: "On an overall basis, we are confident our business should grow on a constant level."

For the year ended June 30, 1996, Tractors Malaysia reported net profit of 91 million ringgit versus 53.9 million a year ago or 28.1 cents a share versus 16.6 cents. Turnover rose to 1.55 billion ringgit from 1.24 billion ringgit during the period.

Oh said that the company was studying the implications of the budget, which was unveiled on October 25. He noted that since the proposal affected imports of new and used equipment, "we may have to shift our strategy somewhat". He noted that the company also has a rental and leasing business.
He did not provide a breakdown of how much contribution the rental division provides to Tractors Malaysia's bottom line.
